case_title: Amrik Singh v. The State of Punjab
neutral_facts: The accused were alleged to have committed robbery and murdered the victim during the course of the robbery. The victim and another individual were proceeding from the office of a sub-registrar when three persons on a scooter attempted to stop them. The scooter driver was blinded by red chilli powder and the scooter was snatched. The accused were identified by the victim as the perpetrators. A recovery of Rs.1 lakh from the accused was also presented as evidence. However, the prosecution failed to establish that the victim and the deceased were carrying Rs.5 lakhs in the scooter's dicky, which was alleged to have been looted. The accused were identified by the victim for the first time in court without a test identification parade, which the court found to be a critical flaw in the prosecution's case.
